benign_causes: Wrong emitter category in the transponder configuration (for example a jet set to A1).
Ground speed derived by MLAT/TIS-B rather than reported by the aircraft.
Exceptional jet-stream tailwind.
alerts.explanation: Ground speed up to 1350 kt in 24 reports, above the 800 kt ceiling for emitter category A3.

benign_causes: MLAT solution jumping between geometries (mitigated by the 1 NM MLAT allowance).
A bad GNSS/INS position from the aircraft (often with a low NACp).
Two aircraft briefly using the same address (see GT-005).
alerts.explanation: Position jumped 2.3 NM in 5.0 s (1592 kt implied, ceiling 960 kt) within one track segment; 20 jumps in this episode.

benign_causes: Formation flight or airshow.
Several aircraft entering receiver coverage together (rare at the same speed and track).
A receiver or feeder reconnecting to the aggregator, so many aircraft reappear at once (they rarely share a velocity).
alerts.explanation: 30 new addresses appeared within 0 s and 10 NM of each other with near-identical speed (about 420 kt) and track: a pattern typical of injected ghost aircraft.

benign_causes: Two aircraft with the same address through a transponder configuration error (addresses are set by hand at installation).
A test bench or ground transponder using a real address.
alerts.explanation: Address ac7e1c was reported at two positions up to 45.3 NM apart at effectively the same time (9 out-and-back jump(s) faster than Mach 3): two transmitters appear to share this address.

benign_causes: Extreme pressure systems (tropical cyclones) or extreme temperatures.
GNSS receiver acquiring or degraded (low NIC), or a faulty altitude source.
Altitude reported in 100 ft steps by older transponders near the band edge.
alerts.explanation: Geometric altitude differed from pressure altitude by up to +8000 ft over 145 s (24 reports), beyond the 3450 ft band allowed for pressure, temperature and geoid effects.

benign_causes: Aircraft transferred to a new State of registry before its transponder address was reprogrammed.
US aircraft re-registered with a new N-number but still transmitting the old Mode S code.
Error in the registration database used by the data source.
alerts.explanation: Registration N12345 is a US N-number, whose Mode S address is a061d9, but the aircraft transmits adfc10 (a United States block).
